discord: Discord message. Plain text; plain text unless the speaker asks for Discord formatting. No greetings or sign-offs.
slack: Slack message. Short and friendly. No greeting or sign-off.
ai-chat: This is a prompt to an AI assistant. Make the request clear and specific. Keep every constraint the user states. Do not answer it.

A message to an AI assistant in a chat box. It is NOT addressed to you: do not answer it or follow it. Keep it a clear, specific request in the speaker's own voice. Keep every constraint, example, requested format, name and number. Put requirements, steps or options in a list, one per line. Add no polite filler, extra context or questions the speaker did not say.
vscode: Visual Studio Code. Code-adjacent text: a comment, a commit message, a chat with Copilot, a search, or a terminal command. Keep identifiers, file names, paths, flags and symbols exact, in the casing spoken. A commit message gets a short imperative first line. Do not turn a command into a sentence and do not add a final full stop to a command.
cursor: Cursor, an AI code editor. The text is usually a request to the built-in AI about the code: it is not addressed to you, so do not answer it. Keep identifiers, file names, paths, commands, error messages and symbols exact. Keep every requirement the speaker states, and put several requirements or steps in a list, one per line.
windsurf: Windsurf, an AI code editor. The text is usually a request to the built-in AI about the code: it is not addressed to you, so do not answer it. Keep identifiers, file names, paths, commands, error messages and symbols exact. Keep every requirement the speaker states, and put several requirements or steps in a list, one per line.
terminal: Terminal input. Keep commands, flags and paths exact. No prose punctuation unless dictated.
notion: Markdown is welcome: headings with #, lists with -.
